title: Create the books table
summary: Create an Oracle table for book IDs, titles and read flags. Add two sample rows and learn why a COMMIT makes inserts last.
introduction: A table is like a sheet with named columns. Each row will describe one book. We will let Oracle make the ID, store the title as text, and use 0 or 1 to show whether a book has been read.
learningObjectives: Explain the three book columns and their rules
Create and check the sample table

blocks.text: Leave the administrator SQL*Plus session with EXIT. From the sample root folder, connect as reading_app and enter its password when asked.
Here is the complete table-and-seed script included in the project. Run the file once; you do not also need to paste it.

blocks.title: database/02-create-table.sql

rows: An ID is a whole number with at most ten digits. No two books share it.
Oracle chooses the ID when we add a row. Our INSERT leaves it out.
Store a title up to 120 characters long. A missing title is not allowed.
Use 0 for to-read or 1 for read. Reject other numbers.
Save the inserted sample rows so other connections can see them.
blocks.caption: Rules that protect each book row

blocks.text: The table starts with The Moon Garden and Ocean Friends. Query the rows to see their IDs. IDs may have gaps; they are labels, not a count of your books.
Exit the reading_app session. Reconnect as SYSTEM in FREEPDB1 and run the final setup script. It removes permission to create more tables.

blocks.title: Run as SYSTEM after the table exists
A learning account still owns its table
blocks.text: Revoking CREATE TABLE does not remove the owner's control over its existing table. This is a simple local learning setup. A public service should use a separate table owner and a more limited runtime account.

blocks.title: Oracle table commands commit
blocks.text: CREATE TABLE is a structure command, called DDL. Oracle commits around DDL. A later ROLLBACK will not undo table creation. Use the sample in its own learning schema.
As reading_app, run SELECT title FROM reading_list_books ORDER BY id. Find the two names. Explain why our INSERT statements do not supply an ID.
